messages.content: Scrivi in italiano una guida tecnica dettagliata di circa 500 parole su come Android gestisce la memoria virtuale. Spiega tabelle delle pagine, fault, file mappati, memoria anonima, zRAM e pressione di memoria. Usa esempi concreti e termina con un confronto ragionato tra le diverse strategie.

Write a detailed tutorial of about 500 words explaining how to design a reliable offline file importer on Android. Cover streaming input, validation, bounded memory, cancellation, atomic publication, resumable work and failure recovery, with concrete examples and tradeoffs.

Design and explain a C++20 bounded producer-consumer queue for an offline inference engine. Include complete code, ownership rules, cancellation, shutdown, worker failures and a worked execution trace. Discuss deadlocks and memory ordering in detail. Aim for a substantial tutorial with four concrete failure scenarios.

Analyze a hypothetical warehouse with three machines and two workers. Each order needs 4 minutes on machine A, 7 on B and 3 on C, in that order. Workers attend only the first and last minute of each operation; machines run unattended otherwise. Design a feasible schedule for six orders, show start and finish times, verify resource conflicts, derive lower bounds and explain whether your schedule is optimal. State assumptions and examine two alternative schedules.

scope: The sustained run used the pre-instrumentation binary; source files changed while it ran. Artifact hashes identify the executed build. Its end-of-run source hash is not a frozen build-source identity.
The old I/O counters may omit final decode reads; corrected bank/drain counters are used only in the subsequent short cache screens.
Two sustained answers reached EOS; the code answer reached the 1536-token cap. The reasoning workload was not reached. No answer-quality evaluation.
No cooldown or within-arm thermal matching in the cache screen. One short A/B/A sequence and one larger-cache screening run do not establish a repeatable speedup.

2816 MiB passed the free-memory estimate but triggered severe major faults and a large slowdown. This rejects free-memory-only admission as sufficient evidence of safe cache residency. 3072 MiB was not attempted after this failure.
No retained scheduling optimization, quantization, APK installation, stock thermal override, model/chat deletion or sustained-five-token/s achievement.

Shared-expert-first is a rejected single-token graph scheduling experiment, not complete per-expert FFN fusion. Plain 2.91/2.79 and candidate 2.76/2.62 tokens/s; all 32 output token IDs agree. No precise slowdown attribution from one short ABBA.
